answer: Fake identities collapse when trust is priced in crystal terms: each agent anchors its reputation with a pearl-weighted bond sized to its claimed web-of-trust depth, a fable the sybil farmer cannot fake cheaply. Ferrous collateral is locked under vesting proportional to vouch edges claimed; if a vouched peer is exposed as a sybil, part of its bond burns instantly. Flooding the network with N fakes costs N bonds plus burn penalties on every vouch chain, while honest agents only forfeit liquidity. Reputation decay makes stolen scores evaporate faster than a farmer recoups stake.
